newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban warplane attacks Afghan town.
newsitem.headline: Taleban warplane attacks Afghan town.

text.p: A warplane belonging to the radical Islamic Taleban militia on Friday bombed the town of Jabal Os-Siraj, where the ousted government military chief is headquartered, but there were no casualties.
The plane flew in from behind the Hindu Kush mountains, attracting a burst of anti-aircraft fire, and dropped a bomb into a nearby field throwing up a cloud of dust at around 7.20 a.m. (0250 GMT).

A Taleban jet fighter dropped three bombs above the town, 45 km (30 miles) north of the Afghan capital Kabul, on Thursday with no casualties. At least 14 people died in an air attack on the village of Kalakan 25 km (15 miles) north of Kabul on the same day.

The forces of ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood, along with those of northern Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, are fighting to retake Kabul from the Taleban, who captured the city on September 27.
